primitives.name: Box–Jenkins Workflow

primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: {'p, q, d': 'integers representing AR, MA, and differencing orders', 'r, s': 'integers representing GARCH parameters', 'ADF': 'Augmented Dickey–Fuller statistic'}
primitives.assumptions: Weak stationarity, normality of residuals, no serial correlation in residuals
primitives.breakdown_regime: Non-stationary time series or heteroscedasticity without proper modeling

primitives.verbatim_quote: **Cointegration/ECM:** Engle–Granger two-step, null of no cointegration, ECM for long-run equilibrium relationships between I(1) series.
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: {'Y_t': 'dependent variable at time t', 'X_t': 'independent variable at time t', '\\pi': 'error correction term coefficient', '\\beta': 'long-run relationship parameter'}
primitives.assumptions: Variables are integrated of order one (I(1)), linear combination is stationary
primitives.breakdown_regime: No cointegrating relationship exists or variables are not I(1)

These methods are foundational in financial modeling but lack novelty or empirical validation. Time series models assume weak stationarity and joint estimation of ARIMA and GARCH components, which are not directly transferable to NFL outcome prediction due to bounded nature of sports data. Cointegration identifies long-run equilibrium relationships among I(1) variables, useful in macroeconomic contexts but irrelevant for discrete event modeling. Risk measures like VaR and Expected Shortfall rely on historical data and distributional assumptions that fail under extreme event scenarios typical in sports.
